You swallow eight spiders a year in your sleep. Except, you don't.
Guess first: how many real cases are on record? Comment a number.

text: Zero. Not one case in science or medicine.

To a spider, you're not a cozy cave. You're a giant, hot, noisy monster.
Your heartbeat, your breathing, your snoring: they all make vibrations.
And to a spider, vibrations mean danger.

text: Your mouth blows warm, wet air at it. Nope!

And if one did walk across your face, you'd probably wake up.

text: Experts say nobody even knows where the eight spiders number came from.
Did you believe it? Yes or no?
